analysis.title: Up 'n' Atom - Nuclear Fundamentals Continue to Improve Despite Weak Stocks
key_insights: TD Cowen sees nuclear fundamentals improving despite lower sector stock prices, which it attributes to the sector's high beta and weakness across broader power-theme stocks. It sees attractive entry points for XE and BWXT ahead of earnings.

The latest NEI survey of U.S. Chief Nuclear Officers shows expectations to add 33.6GW of nuclear generation by 2040, a 44% increase from the 2025 survey. Roughly half is large reactors and the balance SMRs.

The DOE's $17.5B long-lead procurement program has 11 companies submitting expressions of interest, up from 7 originally. DOE said at TD Cowen's Nuclear Conference that 3 to 4 parties have presented highly credible plans.
TD Cowen's sense is that commitments under the DOE program may be approaching, likely involving a group of utilities. An announcement could come by end of 2026 or early 2027.
Poland ordering long-lead items for a large PWR and X-energy's new joint development agreement with AEP add to progress on large reactor and SMR commercial agreements.
TD Cowen expects nuclear companies to keep constructive language on new-build activity in upcoming earnings, with incremental timing commentary the key item to watch.

TD Cowen recently published a deep dive on the nuclear fuel cycle (uranium, conversion, enrichment, recycling) and is most bullish on uranium and conversion. TD colleague Craig Hutchison favors Cameco and Denison Mines.
TD Cowen initiated coverage of LEU (Hold) and OKLO (Hold).

Large reactor pipeline: DOE's conditional $17.5B loan commitment supports long-lead equipment for up to 10 Large PWRs across 5 two-unit projects. Commentary from BWXT, Doosan and CW points to possible long-lead awards by year-end 2026. Doosan notes negotiations on 3 to 5 large units for 2026, some possibly for Europe.
Utilities cite cost-overrun protection as a sticking point on large nuclear builds. TD Cowen sees DUK, AEP, ETR and D as having the most visible activity toward new nuclear.
V.C. Summer: Brookfield was chosen as primary developer for a potential restart of a dual Large PWR project and is negotiating with Santee Cooper, with FID targeted for 1Q28.

Canada: OPG is evaluating technology providers for up to 10GW at Wesleyville. TD Cowen sees CANDU and a Large PWR as most likely, and its ATRL analyst expects CANDU to be favored. Bruce Power is looking at up to 4.8GW (Bruce C) in pre-development.

SMR tracker: channel checks indicate the BWRX-300 under construction at Darlington may be experiencing first-of-a-kind (FOAK) issues. TD Cowen views added cost and delay as possible but still believes BWRX-300 leads SMRs in commercial progress.
Darlington Unit 1 cost estimate is about $14,000/kW. The first Poland and TVA Clinch River units are estimated 2 to 3 years after Darlington Unit 1 comes online.

NuScale's Romania project (RoPower) is reported to have more than 80% of conditions of the February FID unmet. Timeline slipped to 2033/2034 from 2030 and cost is about $6-7B, or about $14,000/kW at the midpoint. The customer will reassess the SMR technology.
Bechtel and TerraPower separated on Natrium after failing to agree on the next phase. TerraPower plans to rebid the EPC contract and says the Kemmerer schedule is unchanged.

Positive project updates: NRC approved TVA's BWRX-300 construction permit at Clinch River after 14 months. Kairos secured $643MM, with Samsung C&T signing as EPC partner. Holtec completed part 2 of its SMR-300 construction permit application.
Oklo management targets a 2028 commercial operation date for Aurora at INL and has admitted it is aggressive. TD Cowen thinks a traditional NRC licensing timeline may mean an early 2030s deployment.
Kairos updated the Hermes 1 deployment timeline from 2027 to 2028, and the NRC approved a latest completion date of April 2029.
The IAEA raised its nuclear outlook for a sixth consecutive year. Its high case reaches 1,284GW by 2060, with SMRs 28% of new capacity additions.

Utility uprate deals: DOE conditional $5B loan to Constellation for about 1.1GW of uprates, DOE conditional loan of up to $4.2B to Vistra for 433MW, Google-Constellation 20-year PPA for 890MW of uprates, and Amazon-Constellation Calvert Cliffs PPA for a 190MW uprate.
BWXT signed a multi-year TRISO fuel contract with Antares. BWXT said no decision has been made on a reported Poland investment, which earlier reports put at $1.5B.

risk_factors: Regulatory delays or rejections of nuclear module designs would hurt the stocks.
Failure to execute on power plant construction or business development plans would hurt stock prices.
A design flaw or issue in a company's manufacturing or supply chain would have negative consequences.
A malfunction at any of the world's nuclear assets could hurt all nuclear companies.
FOAK execution issues at Darlington BWRX-300 could raise cost and delay timelines.
Utilities cite cost-overrun protection as a sticking point on large nuclear builds.
The sector's high beta and weakness in broader power-theme stocks have driven recent price declines.
vol_and_positioning: Sector stocks fell sharply, which TD Cowen attributes to high beta. Over 1M, NuScale was down 23.6%, Oklo 27.3%, NANO Nuclear 22.1%, Terra Innovatum 31.0% and Centrus 19.5%.
Over 12M, NuScale is down 86.3%, Oklo 81.2% and NANO Nuclear 74.3%.
geopolitical: South Korea is targeting $120B in nuclear deployments in the U.S., including 2 APR-1400s and 6 Large American PWRs, through the U.S. Department of Commerce.
Poland's PEJ is beginning long-lead procurement for the first Large PWR unit at Lubiatowo-Kopalino, targeting operation in 2036.
The U.S. government announced a strategic partnership supporting at least $80B of new U.S. reactor construction.

tension_points.bull_case: TD Cowen sees fundamentals improving: the NEI survey shows 33.6GW planned by 2040, DOE long-lead interest rose to 11 companies, and 3 to 4 parties have highly credible plans. It sees attractive entries in XE and BWXT.
tension_points.bear_case: Stocks fell on the sector's high beta and weakness in power-theme names. NuScale, Oklo and NANO are down 74-86% over 12 months. Darlington may have FOAK issues, Romania's NuScale project is reported to have unmet FID conditions, and utilities want cost-overrun protection on large builds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A DOE long-lead commitment slipping beyond early 2027, or earnings calls from nuclear companies that do not carry constructive new-build timing commentary.
